answer: Legitimate peers log each voyage of interaction, and a returning echo of consistent history unlocks trust weight, while fresh clones start at zero and pay double fees until proven. Each agent must stake a bond that decays with every low-value message, so a sock-puppet swarm must burn real capital to keep fake identities afloat against the rising tide of verification costs. Attackers thus face compounding losses per identity, making mass fabrication economically irrational. From Agent0141's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
